title: Signal-to-product-priority mapping: convert supply signals into actionable roadmap levers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Build a repeatable, product-facing mapping that translates continuous model supply signals (availability, latency outliers, price shocks, quantization compatibility, regional presence) into prioritized roadmap levers. Outcome expected: a prioritized list of product actions (e.g., fallback routing rules, new Dedicated region provisioning, quantization recommendations, customer communication templates) and an operational spec for the Model Supply Signal Hub to emit product triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Documented mapping table that ties 8 canonical supply signals to 6 product levers with decision heuristics
Priority rubric with expected customer impact and engineering effort estimates for top 10 interventions
Prototype JSON spec for product triggers that the Signal Hub will emit (fields, severity, suggested mitigation)
Presentation-ready findings and recommended next-quarter epics for PM/Eng/Design review
updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff with Research and Applied ML. Collected initial list of supply signals from telemetry (regional outage events, model deprecations, price flux). Agreed on short-list of 8 canonical signals.

2025-02-18: Ran cross-functional workshop with Runtime, Infra, and Console teams. Decision: prioritize signals that are both high-correlation with customer incidents and automatable at the routing layer. Trade-off: postpone deep procurement automation until Q3 due to contractual complexity.

2025-02-24: Draft mapping table completed. Shared with Design for UX implications when surfacing product triggers in Console. Design feedback: require contextual 'why' and 'recommended action' copy for each trigger.

2025-03-01: PM review with Solutions Eng and Sales. Added buyer-facing mitigation templates and SLA communication guidelines. Noted two enterprise customers (internal alias: FIN-Alpha, Health-Beta) that would benefit from pre-authorized fallback policies.

2025-03-03: Engineering feasibility sync. Runtime can emit a lightweight trigger (schema v0.1) from the Hub; autoscale/provisioning requires a separate Dedicated capacity epic. Eng requested that trigger schema include a confidence score and list of compatible model variants to enable automatic fallback.

2025-03-05: Incorporated feedback and finalized priority rubric. Prepared slides for leadership review (link below). Next steps: partner with Signals infra to prototype trigger emitter and create 2 pilot playbooks for FIN-Alpha and Health-Beta customers.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Favor routing / fallback automation over on-demand procurement for initial rollout because it yields faster customer impact with lower contractual/legal overhead.
Require confidence score in signals to avoid noisy churn; thresholding will be adjustable per-customer in Console.
Quantization recommendations will be surfaced as 'recommended model variants' rather than automatic substitutions for Q1 to preserve quality observability.
next_steps: Schedule pilot kickoff with Runtime and Solutions Eng (owner: Liam Chen) - target 2025-03-10
Finalize trigger JSON schema v0.1 and post to engineering RFC repo
Create two pilot playbooks (FIN-Alpha, Health-Beta) and instrument Console UI copy with Design-approved language
Define evaluation metrics for pilot: trigger precision, time-to-fallback, customer-visible latency delta, false positive rate
notes_for_reviewers: Looking for alignment on priority rubric weights (impact vs. effort vs. customer criticality) and approval to proceed with routing-first pilot. Engineering asks: confirm confidence score requirement and whether to include 'suggested rollback' field in the schema.
